files.name: Travel and Expense Policy 2026
files.content:
Travel and Expense Policy 2026

In effect from 1 January 2026.

1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how employees book business travel and claim business expenses, and how finance decides each claim. It applies to every employee, contractor and intern who travels or spends money on the company's behalf, in every country where we operate. Where a local law or works agreement grants more, the local rule prevails for that country only. Managers are expected to know this policy and to apply it consistently.

Claims are submitted through the expense tool within 30 days of the expense, with an itemised receipt for every line above USD 25. Finance reviews claims monthly and pays approved amounts with the next payroll run. Questions go to the finance operations team, never to the approving manager alone.

2. Approvals

Trips that include a flight need the manager's approval before booking. Trips above USD 5,000 in total also need the department head's approval. Conference registrations above USD 1,500 need the budget owner's approval. An approval covers the trip as described; a change of destination or a longer stay needs a new approval.

Approvals are recorded in the travel tool. An approval given in a chat message or an email is not enough on its own: the traveller must attach it to the trip in the tool. Finance may reject a claim for an unapproved trip in full.

3. Booking

Book flights in economy class for trips under eight hours and premium economy for longer ones. Book through the company's travel agency so that duty of care applies. Rail is preferred to flying for trips under four hours door to door. Personal loyalty points may be kept, but they must never decide which flight or hotel is booked.

Hotels are booked at or below the city's nightly cap in this policy. When a conference hotel costs more than the cap, the traveller may stay there with the manager's approval, and finance reimburses up to the cap only. Extras charged to the room, such as minibar or laundry on trips shorter than five nights, are personal.

4. Meals

Each meal claim covers one day's meals for one employee. Finance reimburses a meal claim up to the daily meal cap of the city where the meals were eaten, as listed below; the part of a claim above the cap is not reimbursed. Business meals with customers follow the entertainment rules instead and are not part of this audit.

Tips are part of the meal and count toward the cap. Meals included in a conference fee or a hotel rate cannot be claimed again.

5. Alcohol

Alcohol is never reimbursable, whatever the city, the occasion or the amount. A claim for alcohol is rejected in full; when a receipt mixes food and alcohol, the traveller files the food as a meal claim and leaves the alcohol out.

6. Ground transport

Taxis, rideshares and public transport on business days are reimbursed in full with a receipt. Car rental needs the manager's approval and the smallest suitable car. Mileage for a private car is paid at the local statutory rate.

7. Receipts

Every line above USD 25 needs an itemised receipt that shows the date, the merchant, what was bought and the amount paid. A card slip alone is not a receipt. A lost receipt may be replaced once a quarter by a signed statement that describes the expense; finance may ask the manager to confirm it.

Receipts in another currency are claimed in that currency; the expense tool converts them at the card network's rate on the transaction date, or the central bank's rate for cash. Claims below show amounts already converted to US dollars.

8. Corporate cards

Corporate cards are for business expenses only. A personal charge made by mistake is repaid within 30 days and reported in the expense tool. Cash withdrawals are allowed only where cards are not accepted, and the cash spent must be claimed with receipts like any other expense.

9. Misuse

Claiming an expense twice, claiming a personal expense or altering a receipt is misuse. Finance reports suspected misuse to the employee's manager and to the compliance team, and recovers any amount paid. Repeated misuse leads to disciplinary action under the employee handbook.

10. Changes to this policy

Finance reviews the caps every December against hotel and meal price surveys and publishes the next year's caps before 1 January. The caps in effect on the date of an expense apply to it; last year's caps are kept in the appendix for audits of last year's claims only.

deliveries.body:
Hi Alex,

Could you pull Q3 paid spend per vendor from the AP ledger export (ap_ledger_2026.csv in the Finance folder)? Q3 means 1 July to 30 September 2026 inclusive. Count only lines with status paid. The export imported some invoices twice: count each invoice_id once. Sum amount_usd per vendor and round to cents.

Please save the result as q3_vendor_spend.csv in the Finance folder, with exactly two columns, vendor and total_usd, one row per vendor that had paid spend, and reply to me with the three vendors with the highest totals.

Thanks,
Mia
